[SAND_HIDDEN_PROMPT][SAND_TRUSTED_AUTOMATION_PROMPT][routine] "Hydria follow-up" (folder hydria-follow-up) is due — Every 2 hours on weekdays, 8:56 AM – 6:56 PM (56 8-18/2 * * 1-5), fired 8/27/2026, 5:06:07 PM.
This is your own routine firing on schedule, not a message the user just typed.
What you saved to do each time:
Finite watch: Hydria / Composite Advanced Technology (via TAS). Tyson wants to know when they reply on the Gmail thread "Re: No internet connection" (thread id 19f6b3c1125d3bf8).

Last known mail: Venkatesh Majeti (m.venkatesh@tasind.com) on 2026-07-31 said they are fine with Option 1 (enable internet egress) but Daniel Campos (dcampos@gohydria.com / dcampos@catecgases.com) has the final decision. Andy had sent two options on 2026-07-21 and chased on 2026-07-30. No mail since July 31.

Related tickets: NETE-740 Hydria Device Access (To Do, Andy; still describes the private-tunnel/OpenVPN path) and NETE-741 Respond to Customer w/ Options (Pending Review).

On each run: look up Gmail tools first (schema may have changed). Search for new mail on that thread or from m.venkatesh@tasind.com, suyash.bhongle@tasind.com, dcampos@gohydria.com, dcampos@catecgases.com, jvega@gohydria.com about Hydria / MQTT / 10.80.1 / no internet. Ignore everything through Venkatesh's 2026-07-31 Option 1 reply.

If they reply (Daniel's decision, more questions, a meeting, anything new), tell Tyson immediately: who wrote, what they said, and whether NETE-740/741 need an update. Then delete this routine.

If nothing new, stay quiet.

Deadline: if this is still running on 2026-09-04 with no reply, tell Tyson the watch expired and delete this routine.
If the instruction mentions a skill (e.g. @Some skill), read that skill file from your workflows folder with Shell and run it as part of this — the mention is a pointer, not a copy.
If the saved instruction spells out a specific MCP tool call, treat its arguments as possibly stale — this routine may have been written long ago — and confirm the current schema with your MCP tool-discovery tool before relying on them.
Carry it out now. If there's something worth surfacing, tell the user how it went with SendToUser — casually, the way you'd mention something you remembered to handle, not by announcing a routine. If the saved instruction above says to stay quiet when there's nothing to report and there's nothing new, just end the run with no SendToUser rather than sending filler like "(no change.)"; nobody is waiting on this. If it can't be done, SendToUser to say why. If you're already mid-task with them, don't stop: finish that first, then slip this in as a "btw …" aside. Keep it self-contained — the schedule asked for this, not the user just now.

You are running this automation as a fresh subagent.
The parent agent's shared durable memories are available in your system context.
Parent transcript pointer: /home/box/sand-data/agent-transcripts/cfde06bf-ba71-4db5-b377-4a6904467ce6/cfde06bf-ba71-4db5-b377-4a6904467ce6.jsonl
Use that pointer only if the task truly needs earlier conversational detail; the parent transcript has deliberately not been copied into this prompt.
Use SendToUser for user-visible updates or results, while preserving the automation's silence contract when there is nothing to report. If you use SendToUser, put the final result there; otherwise the parent thread receives your concise final response.
I'll check Gmail for anything new on the Hydria thread, starting with the current Gmail tool schemas.
Gmail didn’t show up on that first pass — I’ll list the MCP servers and look for mail tools another way.
Gmail is available. Next I’ll pull the current schemas for thread search and get-thread.
Pulling the known thread and searching those Hydria/TAS addresses for anything after July 31.
